paper_metadata.title: Benchmarking Quantum Solvers in Noisy Digital Simulations for Financial Portfolio Optimization

experiments.description: Noiseless QAOA benchmarking on 9-qubit Markowitz portfolio instances, evaluating convergence to the ground-state energy and optimal bitstring identification on a local Qiskit simulator.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA with modified energy-shifted cost function
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient variational circuit with U3 single-qubit gates and ECR entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimized until cost function converges within a reasonable tolerance; reported near-perfect convergence after approximately 600-1000 iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3 assets with 3 binary slices per asset, giving 9 binary variables/qubits; each asset investment zu is encoded in binary as sum_k 2^(k-1) x_i(u,k)
problem_formulation.objective_function: F(z) = theta1 * sum_u r_u z_u - theta2 * sum_{u,v} c_{u,v} z_u z_v - theta3 * sum_u (z_u p_w b - b)^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget constraint enforced via quadratic penalty term
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_i h_i sigma^z_i + sum_{i,j} J_{i,j} sigma^z_i sigma^z_j + delta

problem_instance.description: Synthetic Markowitz portfolio optimization instances generated from randomly created historical price data; 9-qubit case corresponds to 3 assets with 3 binary bits each.

dataset_specification.description: For each asset, initial price generator au,0 sampled from [b/10, b]; historical prices generated as au,l = (1 + alpha) au,0 with alpha uniformly sampled from [-0.25, 0.25]; 100 problem instances generated; theta1=0.8, theta2=0.1, theta3=0.1, b=10

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate synthetic asset prices; compute expected returns and covariance matrix; rescale to QUBO/Ising coefficients; initialize variational circuit parameters
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure energy expectation; compare to exact ground-state energy; identify optimal bitstring from measured distribution

experiments.description: Noisy QAOA benchmarking on 9-qubit Markowitz portfolio instances using a local simulator with controlled two-qubit gate errors, assessing robustness of convergence and return error.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA under controlled CX noise
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient variational circuit with U3 single-qubit gates and CX-based entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimized until cost function convergence within a reasonable tolerance; performance tracked over optimization iterations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 9 binary variables representing 3 assets with 3 bits each
problem_formulation.objective_function: F(z) = theta1 * sum_u r_u z_u - theta2 * sum_{u,v} c_{u,v} z_u z_v - theta3 * sum_u (z_u p_w b - b)^2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_i h_i sigma^z_i + sum_{i,j} J_{i,j} sigma^z_i sigma^z_j + delta

problem_instance.description: Same synthetic 9-qubit Markowitz instances as in the noiseless QAOA benchmark; four representative instances shown in the main text.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic price histories generated from random initial prices and uniform fluctuations in [-0.25, 0.25]; four representative instances used for convergence plots and return-error comparison

noise_model.noise_type: controlled two-qubit gate noise on CX gates

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Synthetic data generation; Hamiltonian construction; noisy local simulation calibrated to IBM Brisbane-like error rates
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute minimum energy deviation and portfolio return error; compare against random-state baseline

results.unit: portfolio return error (reported as exceeding 20 under low noise)

experiments.description: Scalability study of noiseless QAOA on larger Markowitz portfolio instances using a matrix product state simulator for 20- and 30-qubit problems.

algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient variational circuit with U3 single-qubit gates and entangling gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimization over iterations until the cost function reaches a reasonable energy close to the exact ground state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Larger synthetic portfolio instances mapped to Ising Hamiltonians; exact asset-to-qubit mapping not fully specified beyond total qubit counts
problem_formulation.objective_function: Markowitz objective with return, risk, and budget-penalty terms
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian H = sum_i h_i sigma^z_i + sum_{i,j} J_{i,j} sigma^z_i sigma^z_j + delta

problem_instance.description: Two larger synthetic portfolio instances with 20 and 30 qubits used to test QAOA scalability.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic asset data generated similarly to the 9-qubit case; exact asset counts and time-series lengths for these larger instances are not specified

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct larger synthetic Hamiltonians and run MPS-based noiseless simulation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Track convergence of energy deviation versus iteration

experiments.description: QITE benchmarking on IBM Quantum hardware for 9-qubit Markowitz portfolio instances, evaluating return error and optimal bitstring identification under realistic device noise.

algorithm.variant: quantum imaginary-time evolution with variational circuit approximation and ancilla post-selection
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient variational circuit with U3 single-qubit gates and ECR entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: QITE circuit optimized to CQITE < 0.1; text states 4 to 8 layers are required to achieve convergence, with the representative 9-qubit instance requiring 4-8 layers

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 9-qubit Ising encoding of 3-asset portfolio with 3 binary slices per asset; QITE targets the ground state of the Ising Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.objective_function: Markowitz objective mapped to Ising ground-state search
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: budget penalty term in the Hamiltonian; ancilla post-selection used to realize non-unitary imaginary-time evolution
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = sum_i h_i sigma^z_i + sum_{i,j} J_{i,j} sigma^z_i sigma^z_j + delta

problem_instance.description: Same 9-qubit synthetic Markowitz instances as the QAOA benchmarks; representative instance 0 and 50 additional instances are evaluated.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic price histories generated from random initial prices and uniform fluctuations in [-0.25, 0.25]; 50 additional portfolio optimization instances evaluated on IBM hardware

noise_model.noise_type: native device noise on IBM Brisbane, mean ECR error rate around 0.007

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct non-unitary imaginary-time operator e^{-beta H}; embed into a larger unitary via SVD/QR-based construction; optimize variational circuit approximation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Post-select ancilla qubit in |0>; compute return error and measured state distribution; identify optimal bitstring
